findings.evidence: The Requirement says a candidate waiting for checks with mergeable=CONFLICTING moves to integration red gate (integration-repair-pending) and does not stay in blocked-retryable. The T1 design says "No mergeability. The conflict signal stays merge-tree in _prepare. GitHub mergeable is not read." It also says a QueueEnvironmentError leaves the state unchanged. publication_queue.py `_integrate` handles that error with `_note_environment_error` and re-raises. The T1 spec scenario "Derived merge without OpenSpec CLI" requires "its state and attempts are unchanged", which is the PR #837 hang. Only a conflict outside generated files reaches counted integration repair. A generated-only conflict, and any case where merge-tree is not the signal, still hangs in blocked-retryable. The proposal records this narrowing as a coordinator decision (variant A), so the Requirement outcome should be confirmed as accepted. The T2 receipt-preservation path is also never reached for such a candidate.
findings.summary: Requirement item 3 is not met for the conflict case that motivated it. A candidate that conflicts with main and waits for required checks does not move to integration-repair-pending when the failure is a coordinator environment failure. It stays blocked-retryable with only a new reason string. GitHub mergeable=CONFLICTING is not read at all.
